description:
ROTARY CLUB OF MUMBAI KALAKAR

MINUTES OF THE MEETING

Date: 28 October 2026
Venue: Online
Chairperson: President Rtn. Suparna C. M.

1. Members Present

* Rtn. Suparna C. M. – President
* Rtn. Dibyendu
* Rtn. Pooja Mehtaa
* Rtn. Shree
* Rtn. Chandrasekaran
* Rtn. Vaishali – Secretary
* Rtn. Chirag Buddhdev – Joint Secretary

1. Opening and Agenda

The meeting commenced with President Rtn. Suparna C. M summoning the meet.
The National Anthem was led by Rtn. Dibyendu.

Agenda:

1. Rotaract Installation
2. New Projects
3. Club Fellowship
4. Rimjhim – Cultural Fellowship and Fundraising

5. Rotaract Installation

Rtn. Pooja updated the members on her meeting with the Rotaract Principal and Rtn. Smeeta. Rtn Om Chawla offered an orientation session for three teams to encourage registrations.

The proposed installation date from 21 November 2026 within that week . Once finalised, the registration pins and President’s collar will be ordered. The Youth Director, Rtn Poojaa discussed the completed and the upcoming projects & will share the minute-by-minute programme with President Rtn. Suparna.

1. Club Fellowship

Rtn. Dibyendu shared updates on previous fellowship activities organised during Ganesh Puja and Durga Puja, where dignitaries were invited. Members discussed continuing meaningful fellowship activities to strengthen club engagement.

1. Rimjhim – Fellowship with a Cause

The members discussed the proposed Rimjhim event, including its date, venue, budget, and fundraising strategy.

* Proposed date: 20th February, subject to confirmation.
* Venue: Balgandharva, with a rental quotation of ₹42,000. Alternative, more economical venues will also be explored.
* Rtn. Vaishali will be unavailable in March due to a family wedding.
* Rtn. Shree suggested forming a small core committee to finalise the date and venue.
* The preliminary event budget was estimated at ₹5–7 lakh. Finally, we discussed a budget of INR 10L for the same.
* Rtn. Shree offered to raise ₹3 lakh.
* Rtn. Chandrasekaran recommended preparing a detailed spreadsheet outlining expenses and fundraising requirements before finalising the event.

After discussion, members agreed in principle to organise Rimjhim as a fellowship with a cause, celebrating Indian music, art, and cultural heritage while supporting the club’s fundraising objectives with a cause attached to the event.

The members emphasized on maintaining high standards, inviting celebrities, encouraging every member to contribute towards fundraising, and expanding the club’s reach.
A preliminary fundraising target of approximately ₹10 lakh was discussed.

Action Points:

* Finalise the cause by 3rd November 2026, before the Charter Night at MOA Café.
* Explore suitable dates and venues.
* Prepare the detailed budget and fundraising spreadsheet.
* Present the proposal to the Board of Directors for discussion and approval.

1. Vocational Projects and Fundraising

Rtn. Chandrasekaran requested the Vocational Director to prepare a presentation detailing funds raised and utilised, along with proper project documentation.

Members agreed to compile reports of completed projects and a comprehensive list of projects planned for the Rotary year. This documentation will help establish financial transparency and support future fundraising for the vocational centre and other club initiatives.

1. Project Report – Kanya Poojan

Organised by: Rotary Club of Mumbai Kalakar (RCMK) and RCMHV
Project Chair: Rtn. Pooja Mehtaa
Occasion: Navratri

A joint initiative was conducted to support girls from underprivileged communities in Mulund.

* Beneficiaries: 125 girls
* Items Distributed: Stationery and food
* Total Project Cost: ₹35,000
* Contribution by RCMK: ₹25,000

The project brought festive joy to 125 girls through the distribution of essential items.

1. Project Report – Project Annapurna

Project Chair: Rtn. Pooja Mehtaa
Community Project Chair: Rtn. Haima Deshpande
Donors: Mihir Mehta and Jiten Jhuthani

Project Annapurna provided daily meals to families of cancer patients staying outside KEM Hospital during Pitrupaksha and Navratri. The meals were prepared and supplied by ISKCON’s Annamrita initiative over a period of 14 days.

* Duration: 14 days
* Beneficiaries: 200 people per day
* Total Beneficiaries Served: 2,800
* Total Project Cost: ₹1,23,000

The initiative provided essential food support to families accompanying cancer patients during a challenging period, reflecting the club’s commitment to compassion and community service.

1. Conclusion and Vote of Thanks

President Rtn. Suparna C. M. adjourned the meeting after discussions on upcoming projects, fellowship, and fundraising priorities.

The vote of thanks was offered by Secretary Rtn. Vaishali, who expressed appreciation to the President and all members for their participation and valuable contributions.
